instructions:
## Research objective

Your goal is to design adaptive token-ordering strategies for masked diffusion models (MDMs) and compare them to autoregressive models (ARMs) across text and logic-puzzle benchmarks, maximizing accuracy and likelihood via adaptive inference.

## Plan Formulation

- Reproduce and extend experiments showing: (a) training-time hardness for order-agnostic MDMs vs order-aware ARMs, and (b) inference-time gains from adaptive token decoding orders for MDMs.
- Implement three families of studies: (1) text likelihood/scaling-law analysis with π-learners vs ARM, (2) synthetic L&O-NAE-SAT to expose subproblem imbalance, (3) logic puzzles (Sudoku, Zebra) to showcase large accuracy jumps with adaptive inference.
- Adopt a time-embedding-free MDM denoiser pθ(xt) trained with an absorbing-mask forward process; rely on xt itself (mask counts) to implicitly encode noise level.
- Implement adaptive inference oracles that choose which masked positions to unmask next: Top-K probability and Top-K probability margin. Include a stochastic variant (temperature/Gumbel noise) for diversity when generating text.
- Baseline ARMs: train with and without teacher-forced ordering (where applicable) to quantify the benefit of explicit order supervision vs unsupervised adaptive inference.
- Core metrics: text validation loss or generative perplexity, puzzle solve accuracy, and subproblem-level error metrics; additionally track entropy/diversity for text generation.
- Ablations: effect of oracle type (Top-K vs Margin), K (batch size of positions unmasked per step), noise in oracle (temperature/Gumbel), number of reverse steps, positional encodings (learned vs RoPE), and closeness of permutation to identity for π-learners.
- Target model scales: small MDMs (≈6–19M) for puzzles; 170M–1.1B MDMs for text generation; 42M ARM for puzzles; use LLaMA2-7B as an external evaluator for generative perplexity if reproducing that metric.
- Fix random seeds, log all sampling paths and per-step logits; ensure experiments are repeatable across 3+ seeds.

## Data Preparation

- Text for scaling laws and π-learners: use SlimPajama (cleaned RedPajama), sequence length L=2048. Tokenize consistently across ARM and π-learner runs. Use learned positional embeddings (not RoPE) to avoid left-to-right bias unless explicitly testing it.
- π permutations: sample π from three regimes: (a) Unif(S_L) via ≈ L·log L random swaps, (b) 'Closer' via L/10 swaps from identity, (c) 'Much-closer' via sqrt(L) swaps. Persist π used per batch to make runs deterministic.
- Synthetic L&O-NAE-SAT: construct sequences of length L=N+P with N latent tokens over m classes and P observation tokens given by NAE constraints on triples (i1,i2,i3). For the N=20,P=280 setup used in error-imbalance analysis, pad to length 512 by appending a constant token (e.g., value 2) to match model context length used in the paper. Prepare multiple (N,P) settings: (25,275), (30,270), (40,260), (50,250), (100,200).
- Sudoku: use the dataset splits from Shah et al. (2024) for training and in-distribution testing (puzzles solvable by 7 fixed strategies). Prepare a 'hard' test set from the remaining Radcliffe (2020) puzzles requiring unseen strategies and/or backtracking. Represent puzzles as sequences with explicit mask tokens for empty cells; include row/column/box structure via a simple linearization (e.g., row-major).
- Zebra (Einstein) puzzle: use Shah et al. (2024) dataset; linearize each puzzle into a token sequence encoding entities, attributes, and constraints; mask unknowns consistently.
- Text for adaptive inference evaluation: obtain a pretrained MDM on text (e.g., 170M or 1.1B). Prepare prompts for unconditional generation or short-context continuation to sample generations. For external perplexity evaluation, load LLaMA2-7B and implement a likelihood scorer.
- LLaDA 8B (optional extension): if available, prepare coding/math benchmarks: HumanEval-Single/Multi/Split-Line, Math, MMLU, ROCStories. Ensure identical preprocessing as baselines when switching inference strategy.
- Maintain consistent token vocabularies and sentinel/mask token ID across all experiments. Store dataset version hashes and preprocessing scripts.

## Running Experiments

- MDM training (text or synthetic): absorbing-mask forward process with α0≈1, α1≈0; optimize ELBO-equivalent objective over masked positions; time-embedding-free pθ(xt).
- Optimization defaults (TinyLlama-like): AdamW with β1=0.9, β2=0.95, weight decay=0.1; cosine LR schedule with LRmax=4e-4, LRmin=4e-5; sequence length 2048 for text. Use learned positional embeddings for π-learner experiments.
- π-learner vs ARM scaling laws: train causal transformers on permuted inputs π(x) for sampled π regimes; compute validation negative log-likelihood per token; run IsoFLOP sweeps by varying parameter count and tokens seen while holding FLOPs constant; collect best validation loss per compute point.
- Error imbalance on L&O-NAE-SAT: train a 19M MDM with RoPE and max length 512. For each ℓ in 1..N−1, randomly mask ℓ latent and ℓ×(P/N) observation positions; estimate per-position error as squared gap between model log pθ(x|x[M]) and a stronger proxy MDM (same model trained 25× longer). Repeat 1000 times; report latent vs observation position error distributions.
- Adaptive inference oracles for MDMs:
-   - Top-K probability: select K masked positions with highest max_j pθ(x_i=j | x_t).
-   - Top-K probability margin: select K positions with largest |pθ(x_i=j1) − pθ(x_i=j2)| where j1,j2 are top-2 tokens; prefer this when multiple values have similar probabilities.
-   - Stochasticity for generation: add temperature or Gumbel noise ε to the certainty score before Top-K to avoid overly greedy selection; tune ε or temperature on a held-out set.
- Inference loop (discrete reverse steps): start from all-mask; at each step choose S=F(θ,x_t); fill x_s at S by sampling from pθ(·|x_t) (argmax or multinomial as appropriate); repeat for T steps (use 50 steps for puzzles; tune for text). Ensure positions once unmasked remain fixed.
- Sudoku MDM: 6M GPT-2-like architecture; LR=0.001, batch=128, 300 epochs; 50 reverse steps; use Top-K probability margin with Gumbel noise coefficient 0.5 in F. Evaluate solve rate on in-distribution test and hard set.
- Zebra MDM: 19M bidirectional attention model; same LR/batch/epochs; 50 reverse steps; evaluate solve rate with vanilla vs Top-K vs Margin.
- ARM baselines for puzzles: 42M parameter models trained (a) without ordering info, and (b) with teacher-forced sequence-specific order (use provided solving orders if available from Shah et al. 2024). Compare accuracy to MDM variants.
- Adaptive inference on text: with a pretrained 170M–1.1B MDM, generate unconditional samples using vanilla vs Top-K vs Margin oracles; compute generative perplexity using LLaMA2-7B and sample entropy (token-frequency entropy per sequence). Expect lower perplexity with similar entropy under adaptive strategies.
- LLaDA 8B extension: swap inference only (no retraining); evaluate pass@1 or task-specific metrics on HumanEval variants, Math, MMLU, ROCStories; compare vanilla vs Top-K vs Margin.
- Engineering/reproducibility: set seeds; run 3–5 seeds per condition; persist logits at each denoising step; parallelize across GPUs or use mixed precision; log K, temperature/Gumbel parameters, and stepwise certainty distributions. Ensure no reuse of masked positions within the same step and correct handling of mask token ID.

## Results Interpretation

- Scaling laws: plot validation loss vs compute for ARM and π-learners across π regimes; verify degradation as permutation drifts from identity and MDM gap relative to ARM; discuss order sensitivity and multi-task effects.
- Hardness evidence: in text scaling and L&O-NAE-SAT, show that many masking subproblems are harder than left-to-right; quantify imbalance via per-position error distributions (latent vs observation).
- Adaptive inference gains: report accuracy improvements on L&O-NAE-SAT (Top-K Margin vs vanilla), Sudoku (expect large jump from <7% to ≈90% on in-distribution), and Zebra (≈99% for adaptive vs ≈77% vanilla). Highlight Top-K Margin superiority when competing tokens have similar probabilities.
- Text generation: report generative perplexity reductions under adaptive inference with similar entropy; discuss how ordering oracles reduce encounters with hard subproblems during sampling.
- Easy-to-hard generalization (Sudoku): compare in-distribution vs hard set; show adaptive MDM robustness (e.g., ~50% with Margin) vs ARM with ordering (~33%); discuss why order-agnostic training plus adaptive inference helps under distribution shift.
- Ablations: plot performance vs K, reverse steps, oracle noise level; analyze failure cases where oracles pick ambiguous positions; correlate per-step certainty margins with success rates.
- Takeaways: training-time hardness is real, but inference-time adaptivity can plan around it; logits suffice to choose good decoding orders; future work should design better oracles beyond simple Top-K/Margin.

## Report Writing

- Clearly document datasets, model sizes, training configs, and inference details (number of steps, K, oracle noise). Include seeds and hardware.
- Tables/figures to include: π-learner vs ARM scaling curves; subproblem error imbalance (latent vs observation); Sudoku/Zebra accuracy with vanilla vs Top-K vs Margin vs ARM baselines; text generative perplexity and entropy; easy-to-hard generalization on Sudoku.
- Provide concise pseudocode for adaptive MDM inference and oracle scoring (probability max vs margin, with optional noise).
- Show qualitative examples: Sudoku solving trajectories with stepwise chosen cells and certainty margins; text generations with perplexity scores under each inference strategy.
- Discuss limitations (dependence on pretrained MDM quality, oracle hyperparameters, evaluation via external LLM) and propose next steps (learned or self-consistent planners, task-specific uncertainty measures, adaptive K scheduling).
